# FloatFEA — structural results, platform superstructure

**INDICATIVE SIZING SCREEN — NOT A CODE CASE.** Generated by
`scripts/measure/f6_results_report.py`. Every figure below is read from a committed
artifact or computed from the built model; none is typed into the document.

## 1. Scope, and the label this carries

What this is: an FE analysis of the platform **superstructure** under FloatSim's
design-wave loads, with an **indicative** API RP 2A-WSD member check on a
**stand-in** section. What it is not: a compliance calculation, a certification
basis, or a statement that the structure is adequate.

* **Superstructure only.** The buoys, the gimbals' internals and the moorings are
  not modelled here. Shell buckling of the cans is DNV-RP-C202 and is sub-model
  work, exported to CalculiX rather than solved in this tool.
* **Regular design waves at one heading, 0°.** Six periods at a single wave height.
  No irregular sea, no spectrum, no return period.
* **The section is a stiffness stand-in** for a triangulated truss whose depth is
  not decided. Utilisations on it locate the governing members and clauses; they do
  not size steel.
* **API RP 2A-WSD is written for fixed jackets.** Neither it nor ISO 19902 is a
  certification basis for a floating platform. It is used because it is the
  simplest defensible member check, and the locked plan says so in those terms.

## 2. The model

```
bodies                  : 5
  platform              4 members, arm length 50.0 m, 6 nodes
  hub1                  3 members, arm length 25.0 m, 4 nodes
  hub2                  3 members, arm length 25.0 m, 4 nodes
  hub3                  3 members, arm length 25.0 m, 4 nodes
  hub4                  3 members, arm length 25.0 m, 4 nodes
members, total          : 16

the stand-in tube, from the built section:
  D   = 2.5000 m         t   = 0.18000 m
  D/t = 13.8889          r = sqrt(I/A) = 0.822709 m
  A   = 1.311929 m^2    I = 0.887979 m^4
  W   = 0.710383 m^3     W_torsion = 1.420767 m^3
  section class (3.2.3)   : compact   limits 29.1268 / 58.2535 / 845.0704
```

**Each arm is a cantilever from its body's centre node.** The gimbal end bears on a
floating body and is not treated as providing lateral restraint — that is what sets
`K = 2.0` in § 7. Each body is solved independently under **inertia relief**: the
FloatSim joint reactions and the body's own d'Alembert field are applied, the six
rigid modes are removed by Lagrange multipliers, and the equilibrium residual is
reported per case rather than averaged.

## 3. The mass basis, and what is assumed in it

**These are placeholder masses.** Every number in this section is an assumption,
and the utilisations in § 7 scale with them.

```
declared FloatSim override, platform: mass x20.0, inertia {'Ixx': 20.0, 'Iyy': 20.0, 'Izz': 40.0}
mass fraction placed on the arms, f : 0.75

body         total [t]  on arms [t]  remainder [t]  line mass [t/m]  rho_eq [kg/m^3]
platform        2500.0       1875.0          625.0            9.375           7146.0
hub1            1500.0       1125.0          375.0           15.000          11433.5
hub2            1500.0       1125.0          375.0           15.000          11433.5
hub3            1500.0       1125.0          375.0           15.000          11433.5
hub4            1500.0       1125.0          375.0           15.000          11433.5

what the stand-in section could actually hold, at steel density:
  rho_steel x A = 7850.0 x 1.311929 = 10.299 t/m
  platform   assumed   9.375 t/m = 0.910x realisable
  hub1       assumed  15.000 t/m = 1.457x realisable   NOT REALISABLE
  hub2       assumed  15.000 t/m = 1.457x realisable   NOT REALISABLE
  hub3       assumed  15.000 t/m = 1.457x realisable   NOT REALISABLE
  hub4       assumed  15.000 t/m = 1.457x realisable   NOT REALISABLE
```

**The hub arms' assumed line mass does not fit inside the stand-in section.** That
is recorded rather than adjusted: adjusting it would mean inventing a section, and
the whole point of the stand-in is that no section has been chosen. The platform
arms are below the limit and the hub arms are above it, by the factors in the block.

**The platform's rotational inertia is scaled with its mass**, not computed from a
mass distribution. The remainder — the part of each body's mass not placed on the
arms — is carried at the body's own remainder node.

## 4. The loads

```
FloatSim pin             : floatfea-ref-1
provenance tag           : floatfea-ref-1  (HSP-runs)
wave height, full scale  : 24.2 m (0.484 m model, Froude lambda = 50.0)
heading                  : 0.0 deg   -- ONE heading only
integrator               : generalized-alpha, rho_inf = 0.8, dt = 0.01 s, ramp 10.0 s
window                   : DQ6: the last 5 whole periods, starting no earlier than ramp + 10

the associated-period band for H = 24.2 m, DNV practice:
  sqrt(6.5 H) = 12.5419 s    sqrt(11 H) = 16.3156 s

 T_full [s]   H/lambda    vs 1/7   in band   edge offset          basis
       10.0     0.1551  BREAKING        no 20.267% short    sensitivity
       12.5     0.0992        ok        no  0.334% short      GOVERNING
       14.0     0.0791        ok       yes             -      GOVERNING
       15.0     0.0689        ok       yes             -      GOVERNING
       16.2     0.0591        ok       yes             -      GOVERNING
       20.0     0.0388        ok        no  22.582% long    sensitivity

the worst ROOT stress BOUND each case produces, over all sixteen members. This is
the per-component envelope of the total basis: the six components are each
maximised independently over the window, so they do not occur together and the
stress formed from them is an UPPER BOUND, not a stress at any instant. It is the
only quantity in the set that is defined per case, which is why the comparison
below is made on it; the stresses that are checked in s.7 are per-instant.

 T_full [s]   worst ROOT sigma BOUND [MPa]
       10.0                        762.151
       12.5                        483.214
       14.0                        382.531
       15.0                        344.055
       16.2                        330.610
       20.0                        338.226
```

**`T = 10 s` exceeds the deep-water breaking steepness**, so it cannot describe a
real wave of this height. It is reported as sensitivity only, and it is also the
largest of the six on the bound above. `T = 20 s` is outside the band at the long
end. **The governing basis is the four in-band periods.** `T = 12.5 s` sits just
below `sqrt(6.5 H)` by the offset in the block and is kept as the band's lower
edge: across the band the bound falls monotonically as `T` rises, so the lower edge
is what governs and this case is the one that represents it. The monotonicity holds
across the band only — `T = 20 s` ticks back up above `T = 16.2 s`.

**Loads applied:** self-weight, plus the FloatSim joint reactions and each body's
own d'Alembert field over the window. FloatSim is linearised about static
equilibrium, so its multipliers are the **dynamic increment** — the static
weight/buoyancy balance never appears in them and is applied separately here. That
is why § 6 and § 8 can separate a static-only basis from the total.

## 5. Verification — one line per gate

The ladder is ordered by dependency: a failure at a low rung makes the rungs above
it uninterpretable, so each rung is read only on a green rung below. Every ceiling
below is resolved by name out of `floatfea/tolerances.py`, where the single copy of
every numerical tolerance in this repository lives.

| gate | what it asserts | ceiling | constant | status here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G2.1 | every member's element stiffness annihilates its six rigid motions, and has no seventh zero mode | `1.15434e-18` | `PLATFORM_RIGID_MODE_EXACTNESS` | pass |
| G3.1a | each body's assembled mass, centre of mass and inertia against the deck, per body and never on the sum | `1e-13` | `MASS_PROPERTY_AGREEMENT` | pass |
| G4.1 force | per-body dynamic equilibrium over the DQ6 window, force channel, relative to a sum of magnitudes | `2.5e-12` | `F4_G41_DYNAMIC_FORCE` | pass |
| G4.1 moment | the same balance, moment channel, about the point the conventions fix | `0.0002` | `F4_G41_DYNAMIC_MOMENT` | pass |
| G4.4 | the joint mapping conserves force and moment, and reddens on a wrong sign, a wrong node and a dropped internal joint | `1e-12` | `F4_MAPPING_CONSERVATION` | pass |
| EB6 | every buoy and hub label sits where the pinned FloatSim deck says, and a permuted export reddens | `1e-06` | `F4_EB6_POSITION_M` | pass |
| static analytic | the static member forces match hand statics rather than the model, and the tip shear equals the support reaction | `1e-12` | `F4_STATIC_TIP_MOMENT_RELATIVE` | pass |
| G6.1 | every API RP 2A-WSD clause against arithmetic worked by hand in the test, either side of every branch boundary | `1e-14` | `F6_API_CLAUSE_AGREEMENT` | pass |

```
pytest's own summary for each row, at this commit:
  G2.1             2 passed in 0.44s
  G3.1a            53 passed in 0.58s
  G4.1 force       114 passed in 2.30s
  G4.1 moment      114 passed in 2.20s
  G4.4             1 passed in 0.50s
  EB6              2 passed in 0.44s
  static analytic  2 passed in 0.46s
  G6.1             77 passed in 0.54s
```

The two G4.1 rows are asserted by the same module, so their summary lines are the
same line. They are separate rows because they are separate ceilings on separate
quantities, and they are nowhere near each other:
`0.0002` against `2.5e-12` is a factor of `8e+07`,
which is 7.9 decades. The force channel closes to round-off and the moment channel does not,
because the discrete balance carries an `O(h)` lag in the constraint multipliers —
recorded in `docs/load-interchange-v1.md` § 4.1–4.2, which is where the discrete
form was chosen over the continuous one so that this gate means what it says.

**What this table does not carry is each gate's measured residual.** A residual
copied into a second document is a figure whose rule can move underneath it, and
this milestone has already published four figures that were correct when taken and
wrong when read. The residuals are in each gate's own step report, which is
regenerated by rule, and for G4.1 in the output of
`scripts/measure/g41_dynamic.py`.

**Two results from building the clause gate bear on how § 7 should be read.**

```
section 3.2.2(b): where the ELASTIC local-buckling term starts to govern
  F_xe = 2 C E t / D with C = 0.3, against
  F_xc = F_y [1.64 - 0.23 (D/t)^(1/4)], over D/t <= 300

 grade [MPa]   elastic governs from D/t
         235   never, within the clause
         275   never, within the clause
         355   never, within the clause
         420   never, within the clause
         460   never, within the clause
         690                      252.5
  and the stand-in tube is D/t = 13.8889, so F_xc = F_y here
```

So at the assumed grade half of section 3.2.2(b) is inert, and nothing in this
report is reduced by local buckling. The clause is implemented because a section
that *would* be reduced must not pass silently — and it now refuses rather than
returning a number outside its own range.

Second: section 3.3.2 takes the larger of an amplified and a simple interaction
form, and which one governs is not inferable from the loading. § 7 reports the form
per row rather than assuming it.

### The `f` sensitivity

`f` is the fraction of each body's mass placed on its arms rather than at its
remainder node. The shipped value comes off a ladder; this sweeps every rung of
that ladder, plus `f = 1.0`, which is on no ladder and puts the whole body mass on
the members. Each rung is a fresh build and a fresh static solve, and the stress is
the same expression the published CSV uses.

```
ladder                 : (0.75, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1, 0.0)
shipped                : f = 0.75
basis                  : static only -- self-weight, no wave load

     f   root My [N.m]   root sigma [MPa]  sigma / F_b member              
  1.00    1.532813e+08            215.773       0.8104 platform:hub1_arm   
  0.75    1.916016e+08            269.716       1.0130 platform:hub1_arm   
  0.50    2.299219e+08            323.659       1.2156 platform:hub1_arm   
  0.40    2.452500e+08            345.236       1.2967 platform:hub1_arm   
  0.30    2.605781e+08            366.813       1.3777 platform:hub1_arm   
  0.20    2.759063e+08            388.391       1.4587 platform:hub1_arm   
  0.10    2.912344e+08            409.968       1.5398 platform:hub1_arm   
  0.00    3.065625e+08            431.545       1.6208 platform:hub1_arm   
```

**The shipped rung is not the worst rung on this measure, and `f` is not a
conservative choice in either direction.** The root moment rises monotonically as
`f` falls: across the eight rungs above, the static root utilisation spans
`0.8104` to `1.6208`, a factor of `2.00`.
Compare that with § 7's `K` and `C_m` moves, the larger of which is `0.034238` of utilisation —
different bases, so the two are not one ratio, but the difference in order is the
point. The mechanism behind the direction is not isolated here and no cause is
attached to it; what is reported is the sweep.

```
two properties of the sweep a reader will want:
  the dependence is LINEAR in f -- worst residual against the straight line
  through the f = 0 and f = 1 rungs: 8.882e-16 of utilisation
  the four platform arms TIE on the static basis, to 2.384e-13 MPa, so the
  member named in each row is one of four identical ones and not a unique worst
```

## 8. Findings

**(i) The stand-in section governs, and self-weight alone is enough to do it.**

```
worst member-station, total basis : U = 1.7117
  over unity                     : 4 of 32 stations
  bodies they are on             : platform
  stations they are on           : ROOT

and on the STATIC-ONLY basis -- self-weight, no wave load at all:
  worst sigma                    : 269.716 MPa at platform:hub1_arm ROOT
  against F_b = 266.25 MPa        : 1.0130
  against 0.6 F_y = 213.00 MPa   : 1.2663
```

The static root stress on a platform arm is already at the bending allowable before
any wave load is applied. **This is a finding about the SECTION, not about the
platform**, and the locked plan said so in advance: the tube is a stiffness
equivalent for a truss that has not been designed. Nothing was tuned to bring it
under unity, and no tolerance was touched to make it look better.

**(ii) The masses are placeholders.** § 3's overrides, the `f` split and the
platform inertia assumption are declared inputs, and the hub arms' assumed line
mass does not fit inside the assumed section.

**(iii) One heading has been run, and the heading dependence is untested.** Three
of the six force components are IDENTICALLY zero on the static basis, so whatever
those components carry is entirely a function of the one heading that was run:

```
 component  exactly zero on  max |value| on the static basis
         N         48 of 48                 0.0000e+00 N
        Vy         48 of 48                 0.0000e+00 N
        Vz          0 of 48                 6.9488e+06 N
         T         15 of 48                 3.0510e-08 N.m
        My          1 of 48                 1.9160e+08 N.m
        Mz         48 of 48                 0.0000e+00 N.m
```

A heading sweep is the only thing that can exercise those. One consequence is
already recorded in the gate work: part of the moment-channel signal cannot be
exercised by the present case set at all, which makes the corresponding assertion
vacuous rather than passing.

**(iv) `T = 10 s` is excluded from the governing basis** because it exceeds the
deep-water breaking steepness at this height (§ 4). It is also the largest of the
six on § 4's stress bound, so excluding it is the expensive direction — and
reporting it as governing would have meant reporting a wave that cannot exist.

**(v) The truss equivalence is a stiffness equivalence only.** The stand-in tube
stands in for the intended truss in `EI` and `EA`. It does not represent that
truss's local member forces, its joints, or its buckling modes. A member check on
it locates the governing members and clauses, and nothing more.

**Inherited from the FloatSim pin.** Listed because a report that does not name
them invites the reader to attribute them to the structural model:

* **KD-2-revised** — FloatSim pitch natural period 32.34 s vs OpenFAST 26.83 s (+20.54%), attributed to a combined-deck mass-aggregation discrepancy.
* **F-RESONANCE-PEAK-FRAGILITY** — Heave RAO comparison is fragile within +/-25% of omega_n_heave (zeta = 0.057% radiation-only, bare-BEM Q ~ 1000).
* **LATENT: connector attachment transform property test** — test_property_F_ref_equals_T_pullback_of_F_attach fails for extreme inputs (K ~ 1e8 against a 1 nm moment arm) at rtol 1e-8.
* **xi[3:6] interpretation** — FloatSim interprets the rotational state three ways: ZYX-intrinsic Euler (morison.py), axis-angle rotvec (joints.py), and a linearised rotation vector (hydrostatics.py).

## 9. What would change the answer most

In the order I would spend effort:

1. **A mass budget.** Every utilisation here scales with the assumed masses. § 6's
   sweep puts a number on the `f` half of that, and it is linear, so the sensitivity
   to the body masses themselves is of the same order; § 7's `K` and `C_m` moves,
   the two modelling choices one might have expected to matter, are two orders
   smaller. Until the masses are real, the utilisations are a ranking and not a
   magnitude.
2. **The real arm section, or the truss depth.** The governing finding is about the
   stand-in, so replacing the stand-in replaces the finding. A truss of realistic
   depth changes the bending allowable and the governing clause together.
3. **More headings.** One is run, and § 8(iii) measures what that costs: three of
   the six force components are identically zero without a wave, so nothing in this
   report constrains them at any other heading.
4. **An irregular-sea or extreme-value basis.** Six regular waves with no return
   period cannot support a design statement. It would also settle whether API's
   one-third increase applies; it is deliberately not applied here, for exactly the
   reason that these cases carry no declared return period.
